title: AI Actors for UGC Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Choose a named AI actor for a UGC-style product ad. Browse selfie-style presenters by scene, age range and product category, then start with a spoken prompt.
h1: Choose an AI Actor for UGC Ads
lead: Browse on-camera actors by setting and style. Each presenter holds a sample product and delivers a short line straight to camera.
intro: These generated adult presenters are designed for product ads. Choose a setting and a delivery format, then replace the sample product and line with details you can support.

Every card opens the spokesperson workspace with the product photo, sample product description and spoken line prefilled for editing. The people shown are AI-generated actors, not customers or independent reviewers.

Use the directory when the product needs a person to explain one visible detail: a pump, hinge, cap, fit, texture or package reveal. Match the setting to the shopping moment. A kitchen works for a drink ritual, while a desk or podcast room gives a small electronic feature enough space to read on a phone.

The actor links start with a vertical 9:16 composition and a 10-second delivery so you can review a focused first draft. Keep the spoken line to one claim and one action. If you need a six-second hook, a square placement or a longer edit, make that choice in your editor after checking the first result.

Before publishing, compare the generated hands, labels, color and moving parts with the real item. The actor can demonstrate what your source photo supports, but it cannot prove measurements, performance, safety or a result that the photo never showed.

m2.h2: How to make an AI actor video in 3 simple steps
m2.lead: Turn one clear product photo into a spoken vertical ad you can review before posting.

steps.sourceHint: One clear product photo is enough to start
steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. In a bright bathroom, the selected actor holds the sky-blue moisturizer jar toward the camera, then touches one cheek. Natural creator delivery says: "This is the moisturizer step I keep beside the sink." Sound: her voice and quiet bathroom room tone.

items.d: Use one clear product photo with the shape, color and label area visible. A bright, sharp source makes it easier to check the generated hands and product details.
Choose a presenter whose setting fits the product and customer moment. The directory starts a 9:16, 10-second delivery for a focused first draft.
Check the hands, product color and spoken line, then download the vertical draft. Add approved captions, prices or offer dates in your editor before posting.

how_to.d: Start with a clear view of the product and keep its real details intact. Include the full item, the side a shopper needs to see and a label area that can be checked after rendering.

Pick a scene and delivery style that fits the product and audience. Use a close-up for jewelry or skincare details, a room with context for a home tool, and the preset 9:16, 10-second format for a first mobile ad draft.

Use a specific, supportable detail, then review the generated result before publishing. Write one observable feature, one action and a plain next step; read the line against the product page so a generated gesture does not turn into an unsupported promise.
Use the vertical 9:16, 10-second actor draft for TikTok, Reels or Shorts, then check hands, labels and claims before adding captions in your ad editor.
Ask the actor to explain one visible feature or answer one product question. Write the line from approved listing text instead of inventing a customer story.
Start with one hook and one action, then adapt the downloaded clip to the channel crop and add your approved call to action in your editor.
Show one setup or use step with the actor and keep the spoken line tied to the action your source photo supports.

items.d: Do not present a generated person as someone who bought or used the product. Say that the presenter is AI-generated when the ad or platform disclosure rules call for it.

A testimonial must reflect a real, authorized customer statement; do not invent personal experience. For a brand-written line, describe the feature or setup instead of claiming that the actor loved, tested or purchased it.

Do not portray an actor as a doctor or make unsupported health or performance claims. Keep health, fit and performance language tied to evidence in your approved product information, and remove any line you cannot verify.

faq.q: Can AI actors speak in UGC ads?
faq.a: Yes. The spokesperson workspace can generate an actor delivering a short spoken line that you provide.
No. They are generated presenters and should never be described as actual customers.

faq.q: Can an AI actor give a testimonial?
faq.a: Do not invent a customer testimonial. Use real, authorized customer words or frame the line as a brand-written product explanation.

faq.q: How do I create an AI actor product ad?
faq.a: Add your product, choose an actor and delivery style, write a supportable line, then review the result.

faq.q: What format should I use for a first actor ad?
faq.a: Start with the directory's 9:16, 10-second preset for a mobile placement. Review the product details and spoken line first, then make a shorter cut or a different aspect ratio in your editor if the channel needs it.

faq.q: How do I write a safe line for an AI actor?
faq.a: Name one visible feature, show one action and use only a claim you can support. Say what the product does or how it is set up; do not write a fictional review, medical promise or result that requires testing.

faq.q: What should I check before publishing the actor clip?
faq.a: Compare the hands, product shape, label area, color and moving parts with the real item. Check the spoken words against the approved listing language, then add any required AI disclosure, price, caption or offer date in your editor.

faq.q: Can I use an AI actor on a product page?
faq.a: Yes. Use the presenter to explain one visible feature or setup step, and label the presenter as AI-generated when your channel requires it.

faq.q: Can I add captions and an offer after the actor clip?
faq.a: Yes. Download the clip, then add approved captions, prices and offer dates in your editor so the final words match your listing.
